column9: Precise Definitions: Make a conscious effort to understand the mathematical meaning of definitions and the specific role they play in mathematical reasoning. Algebraic and Limit Laws: Keep a running list of the rules that trip you up and revisit them every few days. As you solve problems, pay close attention to how each one is being used. Logical Transitions: Aim to gain clarity on precisely which law is being applied to move from one line of a solution to the next. At this level, random guessing will not suffice; every step must be intentional, purposeful and justified.
column10: Michael Gong, you clearly value learning independently and enjoy working through the handouts on your own. You consistently arrive well-prepared for tests, which demonstrates a strong work ethic.The next level of growth for you will come from engaging your fellow students in deeper discussion or even taking the time to work with a struggling peer. When you do so, I challenge you not to give them easy answers or even hints. Instead, ask them to explain the definitions to you and check their understanding of the theory. In other words, guide them to take the path you took, but allow them to do the heavy lifting themselves. Teaching others in this way will sharpen your own understanding and build your leadership skills.
